body.justification: The theorem identifies the heterogeneous independent-share complexity that determines the multiplicity cost of separate direct temporal rules.
body.gap: Greenaway-McGrevy (2013) is the nearest direct-versus-recursive panel forecasting comparator: it derives asymptotic MSPE expressions for conventional recursive and direct panel-VAR forecasts and ranks them under correct, over-, and under-specified lag orders. An MSPE ranking does not imply the causal TWSF Gaussian-maximum or variance-share frontier stated here; Shen (2026) remains the exact causal-forecasting anchor, while Chernozhukov et al. (2015) supplies only generic Gaussian comparison tools once covariance is known.
body.consumer: The result tells a practitioner when direct TWSF ribbons must widen with horizon and when recursive ribbons retain a constant critical-value scale.
